The purpose of the report before committee today is to request approval to execute partnership agreement with the province of Saskatchewan.
The province in partnership with the cities of Saskatoon, Regina, as well and our respective homebuilders associations was successful in their application for funding under the Code Accelerator Fund.
The Code Accelerator Fund was established by the Government of Canada as part of its action plan to combat climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption.
The fund has three primary objectives.
To accelerate the adoption and implementation of high performance energy codes, promote higher compliance rates with adoptive codes,
and build capacity and support market readiness for ambitious code adoption.
The program has approximately 30 million available until March 31st, 2027.

The total funding provided to the city through the agreement is $3,775,417, which will be used to hire a temporary full-time energy code specialist who will work with the province and the city of Saskatoon and our project partners to support key outcomes of the project.

These include creating supportive education programs for builders and tradespeople, developing a Saskatchewan energy code guide, and formulating a strategy and roadmap to advance the adoption of energy performance tiers.
The noted project outcomes also support the initiatives that are contained within the city of Saskatoon level mission community plan.

On an annual basis, administration presents a report requesting council approval of the current year adjusted and next year preliminary prepaid servicing rates.

Administration has reviewed the actual 2023 costs of land developed by the city as well as the 2024 tenders received and changed in standards in order to establish the proposed adjustment to 2024 off-site and direct services and set the preliminary rates for 2025.
The city does not allocate general revenues to be used for funding initiative for funding infrastructure for land development.
The financial source of revenue for construction of infrastructure for land development in new areas within the city is the prepaid.

8th Service Rates. The prepaid rates are divided into two major servicing categories, direct services, which benefit the frontage of the property, and offsite services, which benefit the neighborhood or catchment area as a whole. The proposed rates in this report were discussed and received by Saskatoon land, corporate financial services department, as well as with members of the developers liaison committee that utilize these rates. The proposed rate increases were required to generate the revenue needed to meet the projected and actual expenditures for cost recovery.

The overall inflationary pressures that have been evident the past three years have softened with inflation stabilizing between the targeted 1% to 3% range at the end of the construction season. The overall proposed prepaid rates for 2024 for the recovery of cost for residential property is a 1% reduction compared to a minus 1.3% for direct services and minus 0.5% for offsite services.

This compares to the overall prepaid service rate change in 2023 for the recovery of cost for residential properties of 6% comprised of 6.5% for direct services and 5.1% for offsite services. The prepaid rate changes by zoning area are attached in appendix 1 and appendix 2 provides details on the prepaid service rate evaluations.

The proposed changes for administration of land development program to account for changes in standard collective agreements and car allowance rates is between 2.6% and 3.7% compared to between 3.0% and 6.5% in 2023.
The purpose of adjusting the prepaid rates is to recover the cost of providing prepaid services for the preparation of service lots for sale in Saskatoon.
